serp_review.observation: Results: blog.incogni.com (two iPhone/phone deletion guides), behance.net gallery, techloy.com, nira.com, geeksforgeeks.org and low-quality aggregator pages. The search summary showed conflicting answers: one guide says touch and hold then add messages, one says tap the avatar for checkboxes, one describes 'Edit' then 'Select all' (Apple Mail-style controls), one says the 50-message batch limit means using a desktop browser for large deletions, and one claims the native app has no select-all. Some results cover Apple's Mail app rather than the Gmail app.
serp_review.limitation: One standard US web search; individual result pages weren't opened, so the competitor characterisation rests on titles and snippets only.

information_gain: A source-checked, Gmail-app-specific (not Apple Mail) procedure that puts search first, makes the documented 50-message default actionable with a rounds table (selected count to Select all taps, and where a computer is the better tool), contrasts it with the desktop all-matching banner, and gives an app-identification table that resolves why other guides' Edit/Select All steps don't match the Gmail app. Published guides (how-to-bulk-delete-gmail-emails, delete-all-emails-from-one-sender-gmail) explicitly say the iPhone/iPad app 'was not reviewed here'; the hub how-to-select-all-emails-gmail is desktop-only.
overlap_check: No published page covers the iPhone Gmail app. Adjacent overlap: how-to-bulk-delete-gmail-emails has an Android 50-batch FAQ, gmail-select-all-conversations-not-showing has one line on mobile, and the deferred delete-all-emails-gmail-app-android topic is Android. The draft links to the hub and the troubleshooting page instead of repeating desktop steps. A reviewer could reasonably ask whether a short iPhone section in the hub would be enough; the SERP confusion between apps and the rounds table are the case for a standalone page.
limitations: Source and documentation review only; no live iPhone or Gmail mailbox test, and no original screenshots.
The fetch tool summarised rather than quoted the iOS 'Delete multiple messages quickly' steps; exact UI labels and the accumulate-then-delete order should be confirmed on the live page or a device.
The rounds table is arithmetic from Google's documented 50-message default, not a timed or observed test; the 'better tool' thresholds are editorial judgement.

Apple Mail behaviour wasn't reviewed (Apple's article text couldn't be fetched); the draft makes no Apple Mail procedural claim and only reports that several search results describe Edit-first controls.
Whether the Gmail iPhone app offers an all-matching selection beyond batches is stated only as 'not described in Google's help', not as tested absence.
SERP review relied on result titles/snippets, not opened pages.
